13. Based on the evidence led before this court, the issue-wise finding in the matter is as under.

Issue No. (i) and (ii)
(i) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to recovery of Rs. 11,70,100/- from the defendant, as claimed in the plaint?
OPP (ii) Whether the plaintiff is entitled for interest, if so, at what rate and for which period?
OPP 14.
At the outset, I may note that defendants, in their written statement do not dispute that they received an amount of Rs. 11,70,100/- in their bank account.
The relevant entries in the bank account (totaling Rs. 10,70,100/- Ex. PW1/1) have been tabulated in table-I noted above and the same is reproduced hereinafter for easy reference.
Since the said entries including the amount and date of transfer are undisputed, therefore, it is proved on record that defendants received a total amount of Rs. 11,70,100/-.
TABLE-I S. No. Date

4 3. 19.12.2015 15,000/- Komal Chand Jain 4. 19.12.2015 15,000/- Komal Chand Jain 5. 19.12.2015 15,000/- Usha Jain 6. 19.12.2015 15,000/- Usha Jain 7. 07.07.2016 3,00,000/- Usha Jain 8. 29.07.2017 2,00,000/- Usha Jain
15. Now, the only dispute between the parties is as to whether the said money was a loan transaction or was it transferred as household expenses by the plaintiff herself out of her own free will.
16. Before, proceeding further, I may note that plaintiff, apart from her, had produced her mother Rekha Thakur and her friend Sabir Malik as witnesses before this Court.
The testimony of the said two witnesses is beyond pleadings.

The entire pleadings of the plaintiff are silent on the point that any of the said witnesses were witness to the loan transaction between plaintiff and defendants/in-laws and thus, the said testimony cannot be read in evidence.
17. This leaves the sole testimony of plaintiff/PW-1 as the only oral evidence to show that the transactions set up are loan transactions.

Plaintiff has asserted this fact in her oral testimony in her affidavit in evidence Ex. PW1/A.
18.

Nothing has come out from the cross-examination of the said witness to suggest that the money transferred to the account of defendants was not a loan transaction or it was transferred as contribution of plaintiff to household expenses.
If one peruses the amount being transferred on different dates into the accounts of defendants, the money transferred is in lump sum and in large sums.
The same would suggest that possibly the money was being asked by the defendants from plaintiff for some purpose and not as household expenses.

Household expenses are usually recurring in nature and the frequency and the amount transferred does not show any recurring pattern of transfer or a fixed amount to suggest that they are household expenses.

19. In my humble opinion, the said testimony of plaintiff is sufficient to shift the onus towards the defendants to show that the money transferred by plaintiff to the account of the defendants was not a loan transaction; but it was transferred by plaintiff on her own for contributing towards household expenses.

sentences.text: I may note that D-1 did not step in the witness box and D-2 expired before his evidence could be recorded.
The defendants only caused the testimony of DW-1/Shashank Jain on the point that the money transferred to the account of the defendants was towards household expenses.
21. In my humble opinion, the testimony of Shashank Jain is not sufficient to shift back the onus on the plaintiff qua the recovery sought.
A perusal of table-I would show that all transactions (except at S.No. 3 and 4) are in favour of D-1/Usha Jain and they are major money transactions.
Even the transaction mentioned at S.No. 3 and 4 of table-I in favour of D-2/Komal Chand Jain are dated 19.12.2015 and they cumulatively amount to Rs. 30,000/-.
On the same day i.e. 19.12.2025 another sum of Rs. 30,000/- (by way of two other transactions) was transferred to D-1/Usha Jain.

It is difficult to accept that such lump sum money would be transferred by plaintiff into the account of her in-laws for household expenses when her total income at that time was ranging between Rs.
45,000/- to Rs. 50,000/- only i.e. much beyond the income of plaintiff.

22. In fact, it does not appeal to logic that payments mentioned at S.No. 7 to 10 of table-I (which range from Rs. 1.5 lac to Rs. 3 lac) would be for household expenses when, as per DW-1/Shashank Jain, the total household expense of the parties at the relevant time was only Rs. 2 lac.

In this regard reference can be had to cross-examination of Shashank Jain dated 17.07.2025 wherein he claims that in the year 2015 to 2017, the total earning of the family was Rs. 4 lac, excluding the earning of the plaintiff and the monthly family expense were about Rs. 2 lac.

It does not appeal to logic that a family which earns more than Rs. 4 lac per month (excluding the income of plaintiff) would require large contributions ranging from Rs. 1.5 lac to Rs. 3 lac on different occasions towards household expenses.

23. Many of the payments noted in table-I above are done on the same date and thus, it does not appear reasonable that such bulk money transfer was being made by plaintiff to her in-laws as household expenses.

As noted above, household expenses are usually recurring in nature and if plaintiff was contributing towards the said expenses, even if intermittently, the same cannot be large sums of money found transferred in the account of the defendants.
24. Thus, if I consider the above facts, in my humble opinion, the money transferred by the plaintiff to the defendants appear to be loan transactions.

25. But, save and except transaction No. 8, 9, 10 done in the account of Usha Jain dated 29.07.2017,
all other transactions detailed at S.No. 1 to 7 of table-I are barred by time.
All transactions mentioned at S.No. 1 to 7 pertain to period 16.11.2015 to 07.07.2016.
The present suit has been filed only on 28.07.2020.
26. Under Article 19 of the Limitation Act, 1963, a period of 3 years has been prescribed for recovery of money payable for money lent.
The said period of limitation begins to run when the loan is made.
27. Thus, for each of the 7 transactions noted at S.No. 1 to 7, the limitation began to run on the day when the money was lent and after expiry of 3 years therefrom, limitation expired.

Since the present suit has been filed after expiry of 3 years for each of the said 7 transactions, plaintiff cannot be Bhumika Thakur vs Usha Jain on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181807547/
6 allowed to recover the said money from defendants.

28. At best, she is entitled to recover for 3 transactions only i.e. the transactions mentioned at S.No.
8 to 10 with each transaction dated 29.07.2017 amounting to Rs. 5.5 lac in total.
This money was given to D-1/Usha Jain.

Thus, plaintiff can only recover the said money from D-1.
29.
As far as claim of interest is concerned, neither it is pleaded nor there is any evidence to show that plaintiff was promised any interest on the aforesaid amount.
Thus, at best, plaintiff can recover interest from the date of filing of the present suit till realization on the amount of Rs. 5.5 lac.

Considering the advance age of D-1 and the relationship between the parties, in my humble opinion,
interest of justice shall be served in case plaintiff is awarded simple interest @ 4% per annum on the amount of Rs. 5.5 lac, from the date of filing of the present suit till realization.

30. Before parting, I may note that even though plaintiff claims that she transferred a sum of Rs. 1.6 lac to D-2/Komal Chand Jain till 08.01.2018, she only placed on record her account statement showing a transfer of sum of Rs. 30,000/- (detailed in S.No. 3 and 4 of table-I) to Komal Chand Jain/D-2.

On the other hand, defendants caused production of bank account of K.C. Jain/D-2 for the period 01.01.2018 to 30.06.2018 Ex. X (for Yes Bank account) where there is no receipt of money from plaintiff for 08.01.2018.
Thus, only an amount of Rs. 30,000/- was shown to have been transferred by plaintiff to D-2 and that sum has already been found to be barred by time.
Thus, the entire claim of the plaintiff qua D-2 is liable to fail.
31. Accordingly, the issues under consideration are partly decided in favour of plaintiff in terms indicated above.
1. Plaintiff is entitled to recover a sum of Rs. 5.5 lac from D-1 only with simple interest @ 4% per annum from the date of filing of this suit i.e. 28.07.2020 till realization.
She is entitled to costs of the suit to be recovered from D-1 only.
2. Plaintiff's claim qua D-2 is dismissed.
32. Let a decree sheet be prepared accordingly.
